items.title: A principal ideal domain is normal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a principal ideal domain is normal, that is, integrally closed in its fraction field (statement lines 8282-8285). The proof does not use unique factorization: it cancels the common factor of a fraction to reach the coprime case and then reads an integrality relation as a divisibility statement forcing the denominator to be a unit (proof lines 8287-8296). Using only that the ring is a principal ideal domain, rather than that it is a UFD, is what distinguishes this argument from the general one. H2.
